Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None turned up on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.
2. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 08.03.2022.

3. While arguing the second bail application, the counsel for the applicant argues that the FIR in question was registered alleging that on 26.02.2021 at about 12.30 PM when the daughter of the informant aged about 11 years was coming home on a cycle, the applicant enticing her to get a Cake,
Satyam Srivastava vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148246897/
1 took her in a private place and inserted finger in the private part of the victim.
4. In view of the said allegation, which was supported by the statements under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the applicant apprehended and is being tried for the offence in question.

sentences.text: The counsel for the applicant further argues that the medical examination of the victim was specifically denied by the informant and the mother of the victim, as such, apart from the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., and the FIR, there was no material to corroborate the allegation against the applicant.

She draws my attention to the affidavit executed by the informant and as contained in the Anneuxre No. 3, wherein the informant had deposed that she did not get the medical examination of the victim done nor does she was to get it done.
She also stated that she wants to end the litigation which was instituted on account of pressure.
In the light of the said, the counsel for the applicant further argues that during statement recorded during trial, the informant admitted that she had refused the medical examination of the victim.
During trial the informant admitted the signature on the affidavit, relied upon by the counsel for the applicant and as contained in Annexure No. 3.

The counsel for the applicant has further placed across the bar a copy of the order sheet, which demonstrates that despite the order of stopping the salary of the P.W. 3, he is not forthcoming for deposing.
The counsel for the applicant further argues that the applicant is languishing in jail since 27.02.2021 having no criminal history, as such, he may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the victim was aged about 11 years and considering the gravity of the allegation, the second bail application filed by the applicant deserves to be rejected.
6.

Considering the arguments as recorded above, while rejecting the first bail application, this Court had noticed the allegation in the FIR and the two statements, however, the fact that there is no medical on record was not noticed.

Apart from the fact, there is no medical on record, which was specifically refused by the informant and the victim, the case is based only upon the statements under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the assertion in the FIR gets partly divested in view of the subsequent affidavit signed by the informant and duly accepted during examination at the time of trial.
Apart from these facts, primarily the mandate of Section 35(2) of the POCSO Act has also been violated in the present case.

Further considering the conduct of P.W. 3, who is not coming forward for deposition despite an order stopping his salary, clearly demonstrates that there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in the near future.

Considering all these facts coupled with the applicant has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Satyam Srivastava be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 36 of 2021, under Section 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Husainganj, District Lucknow, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
